correctness.rationale: Polynomial affine precision and facet exposing-function positivity imply every denominator vanishes on each factor residual cylinder. For no-parallel m-gons the m−3 distinct residual intersections on every side line force least vanishing polynomial degree m−3; for central m-gons the m−4 residual intersections force m−4; for nonparallelogram quadrangles any residual point forces degree 1. Planar Wachspress adjoint achieves these degrees. For a top-degree monomial of any nonzero q in each extended residual ideal, its coefficient under expansion in all other blocks belongs to the ideal, forcing its degree in each block to be at least the corresponding minimum; summation gives degree ≥ Σδ_i, and tensor product Wachspress coordinates attain it. Exact arithmetic checker verified five factor shape classes and product affine precision; it is supplementary, not an infinite proof. No unstated genericity beyond eligible shape conditions.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The prior 2026 construction proves deg_GBC(product) ≤ Σ degree_i, and the 2025 adjoint result proves the corresponding product adjoint has exactly that degree. Even combined with planar deg_GBC(P_i)=degree_i, these statements leave open a non-product barycentric system of lower common denominator degree. It is therefore neither a rephrasing nor an immediate logical corollary of the inspected statements.

value.rationale: A motivated structural sharp minimum-denominator theorem for all products of quadrilaterals and two wide geometric polygon classes. In particular, products of k nonparallelogram quadrangles exhibit exact algebraic complexity k despite universal conjectural m−2d bound zero, supplying an arbitrarily large nontrivial gap. This is not a mere product upper bound, numerical table or single degenerate example; it distinguishes geometry and excludes hidden cancellation across factors.
